translations.text: The word of the Lord that came to Joel son of Bethuel.
Hear this, elders, and listen, all inhabitants of the land. Has anything like this happened in your days or in the days of your ancestors?
Tell your children about it, and let your children tell their children, and their children another generation.
What the devouring locust left, the flying locust ate; what the flying locust left, the crawling locust ate; and what the crawling locust left, the cricket ate.
Wake up, drunkards, and weep! Wail, all you wine drinkers, over the wine that has been taken from your mouths.
For a nation has come up against my land, mighty and beyond counting. Its teeth are like a lion’s teeth, and its fangs like the fangs of a young lion.
It has devastated my vine and stripped my fig tree. It stripped it bare and threw it away, and its branches turned white.
Lament like a virgin dressed in sackcloth over the husband of her youth.
Fine flour and drink offerings have disappeared from the house of the Lord. Kings sit in mourning, along with the priests who minister to the Lord.
The field has been ravaged, and the land sits in mourning, because the grain has been ravaged, the wine has dried up, and the olive trees have been ruined.
Be ashamed, farmers, and wail, vine growers, over the wheat and barley, because the harvest of the field has perished.
The vine has dried up, and the fig tree has withered. The pomegranate trees, palm trees, apple trees, and all the trees of the field have dried up, because joy has ceased among humankind.

Priests, dress yourselves in sackcloth and dance! Wail, ministers of the altar! Come in and spend the night in sackcloth, ministers of my God, because fine flour and drink offerings have been withheld from the house of your God.
Consecrate a fast; call an assembly. Gather together, elders and all inhabitants of the land, at the house of the LORD your God. Cry out to the LORD your God and say:
Alas, alas for the day! For the day of the Lord is near, and devastation will come from God.
Look! Food has disappeared before our eyes, and joy and rejoicing from the house of our God.
The heifers are parched at their mangers. The storehouses are ruined, the presses are demolished, and the grain has dried up.
Why do the livestock groan, and the herds of cattle cry? Because they have no pasture. Even the flocks of sheep have perished.
To you, Lord, I cry, because fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness, and flame has burned all the trees of the open country.
Even the wild animals cry out to you, because the streams of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness.
Blow the trumpet in Zion and shout on my holy mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, because the day of the Lord has arrived and is near.

A day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness! Like dawn spreading over the mountains comes a numerous and mighty people. Its like has never existed, nor will there be anything like it afterward, through the years of generation after generation.
Before it fire devours, and behind it a flame burns. Before it the land is like the garden of Eden, but behind it is a desolate wilderness, and nothing escapes it.
Its appearance is like the appearance of horses, and they run like horsemen.
Like the sound of chariots bounding over the mountaintops, like the sound of a fiery flame consuming stubble, and like a mighty people drawn up for battle.
Peoples will tremble before it, and every face will turn black like soot on a cooking pot.
They will run like mighty men and climb the walls like warriors. Each will go his own way, and they will not turn aside from their paths.
They will not push one another, but each will go along his own path. They will fall under the weight of their weapons and will not rise up.
They will climb into the cities, run along the walls, climb onto the houses, and enter through the windows like thieves.
Before him the earth was shaken and the heavens trembled. The sun and moon grew dark, and the light of the stars faded.
The LORD raises his voice before his army, because his camp is very large, and the one who carries out his command is mighty. For the day of the LORD is great and very terrifying. Who can endure it?
Now, says the Lord, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping, and mourning.
Tear your hearts and not your clothes, and return to the Lord your God, for he is merciful and compassionate, slow to anger and abundant in kindness, and he turns back calamity.
Who knows whether he will turn back and have mercy on us, leaving a blessing behind him, flour and a drink offering for the Lord your God?
Blow the trumpet in Zion; consecrate a fast; call an assembly.
Gather the people; consecrate the assembly. Gather the elders, and gather the young and the nursing infants. Let the bridegroom come out of his room and the bride out of her bridal chamber.

Between the porch and the altar, let the priests, the Lord’s ministers, weep and say, “Spare your people, Lord, and do not hand your inheritance over to disgrace and the rule of the nations, so that the nations will not say, ‘Where is their God?’”
Then the Lord became zealous for his land and had pity on his people.
The LORD answered and said to his people, “Look, I am sending you grain, wine, and oil so that you may be satisfied. I will no longer make you an object of disgrace among the nations.”

I will drive the northerner away from you and push him into a thirsty and desolate land, his front toward the eastern sea and his rear toward the western sea. His odor will spread and his stench will rise, because he has risen up to act.
Do not be afraid, land; rejoice and be glad, for the Lord has risen up to act.
Do not be afraid, wild animals, for vegetation has sprouted in the wilderness pastures. The tree has borne its fruit, and the vine and the fig tree have yielded their abundance.
Children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, who has given you food in righteousness and sends down rain for you, the early rain and the late rain, as before.
The threshing floors will be filled with grain, and the presses will overflow with wine and oil.
I will repay you for the years that the flying locust, the crawling locust, the cricket, and the devouring locust ate—my great army that I sent against you.
You will eat and be satisfied, and you will praise the name of the Lord your God, who has done wonders for you. My people will never be put to shame.
You will know that I am in the midst of Israel. I, I am the LORD your God, and there is no other besides me. My people will never be put to shame.
Afterward I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your elders will dream dreams, and your young men will see visions.
Even on male slaves and female slaves I will pour out my Spirit in those days.
I will perform wonders in heaven and on earth: blood, fire, and clouds of smoke.
The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and dreadful day of the Lord comes.
Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved, for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as the Lord has said, for the survivors whom the Lord has called.
For in those days and at that time, when I bring back the captives of Judah and Jerusalem,

I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment with them over my people and over Israel, my inheritance, who were scattered among the nations, because they divided my land.
They cast lots for my people, gave boys as payment for prostitutes, and sold girls for wine, which they drank.

What do you have against me, Tyre and Sidon and the whole region of Philistia? Are you repaying me for something? If you inflict harm on me, I will swiftly and speedily bring your repayment back upon your own heads.
Because you took my silver and my gold and brought my beautiful vessels into your temples.
You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, to remove them far from their own territory.
Look, I am rousing them from the place to which you sold them, and I will bring your repayment back upon your own heads.
I will hand your sons and daughters over to the people of Judah, and they will sell them to Sheba, to a distant nation, for the Lord has spoken.
Proclaim this among the nations: Consecrate the war! Rouse the warriors! Let all the fighting men draw near and advance!
Beat your plowshares into swords and your sickles into spears. Let the weak say, “I am a warrior!”
Gather and come, all you surrounding nations! Draw near! There the Lord will shatter your might.
Let the nations rouse themselves and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
Sharpen the sickles, for the harvest is ripe. Go in and tread, for the vats are full and the winepresses overflow, because their wickedness is great.
Multitudes upon multitudes in the valley of decision! For the day of the Lord is near in the valley of decision.
The sun and moon have grown dark, and the light of the stars has faded.
The Lord will roar from Zion and raise his voice from Jerusalem, and heaven and earth will shake. The Lord will have compassion on his people and strengthen the people of Israel.
You will know that I am the Lord your God, who dwells in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, and foreigners will no longer live in it.

On that day the mountains will drip sweetness, the hills will flow with milk, and all the channels of Judah will flow with water. A spring will come out from the house of the Lord and water the Valley of Shittim.
Egypt will become a ruin, and Edom a desolate wilderness, because of the violence against the people of Judah, for they shed innocent blood in their land.
Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
I will avenge their blood and will not pardon. The Lord dwells in Zion.
